results.name: decade_shared_contrast
results.description: Yes rate for non-example targets sharing a tens digit with some example minus yes rate for targets sharing none (among sets of >=2 examples); observed below null means the model over-weights local magnitude neighbourhoods relative to people.
results.code:
# name: decade_shared_contrast
# description: Yes rate for non-example targets sharing a tens digit with some example minus yes rate for targets sharing none (among sets of >=2 examples); observed below null means the model over-weights local magnitude neighbourhoods relative to people.
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",")
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    mat = np.full((len(df), 4), -1)
    for j in range(4):
        mat[:, j] = pd.to_numeric(s.str[j], errors="coerce").fillna(-1).astype(int).values
    valid = mat > 0
    n = valid.sum(1)
    shown = np.any(valid & (mat == t[:, None]), 1)
    dec = np.any(valid & (mat // 10 == (t // 10)[:, None]), 1)
    r = df["rating"].values
    a = (n >= 2) & ~shown & dec; b = (n >= 2) & ~dec
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: target_100_yes
results.description: Yes rate for target 100 across all sets not containing 100; observed above null means people over-accept the salient endpoint 100 relative to the model.
results.code:
# name: target_100_yes
# description: Yes rate for target 100 across all sets not containing 100; observed above null means people over-accept the salient endpoint 100 relative to the model.
def test_statistic(df):
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    has = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.contains(r"(^|,)100($|,)").values
    m = (t == 100) & ~has
    return float(df["rating"].values[m].mean()) if m.any() else 0.0

results.name: participant_set_consistency
results.description: SD across participant x set blocks (>=5 non-example trials) of the participant's yes rate on that set; observed above null means people commit to one hypothesis per set (responses within a set are more correlated than the model's shared-probability answers).
results.code:
# name: participant_set_consistency
# description: SD across participant x set blocks (>=5 non-example trials) of the participant's yes rate on that set; observed above null means people commit to one hypothesis per set (responses within a set are more correlated than the model's shared-probability answers).
def test_statistic(df):
    pid = (df["trial_index"].values == 0).cumsum()
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    ex = sets.str.split(",")
    shown = np.array([str(a) in b for a, b in zip(t, ex)])
    g = pd.DataFrame({"pid": pid, "s": sets.values, "r": df["rating"].values})[~shown]
    a = g.groupby(["pid", "s"])["r"].agg(["size", "mean"])
    a = a[a["size"] >= 5]
    return float(a["mean"].std())

results.name: rule_set_member_far_outspan
results.description: Yes rate for targets >10 outside the example span that are multiples of k (k in 3..11) when all examples (>=3) are multiples of k; observed above null means the model under-generalises a clear arithmetic rule beyond the examples' span.
results.code:
# name: rule_set_member_far_outspan
# description: Yes rate for targets >10 outside the example span that are multiples of k (k in 3..11) when all examples (>=3) are multiples of k; observed above null means the model under-generalises a clear arithmetic rule beyond the examples' span.
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",")
    lens = s.str.len().values
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    mat = np.full((len(df), 4), -1)
    for j in range(4):
        col = s.str[j]
        mat[:, j] = pd.to_numeric(col, errors="coerce").fillna(-1).astype(int).values
    valid = mat > 0
    mn = np.where(valid, mat, 1000).min(1); mx = np.where(valid, mat, -1).max(1)
    out = ((t < mn - 10) | (t > mx + 10))
    hit = np.zeros(len(df), bool)
    for k in [3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11]:
        allk = np.all(~valid | (mat % k == 0), axis=1)
        hit |= allk & (t % k == 0)
    m = hit & out & (lens >= 3)
    return float(df["rating"].values[m].mean()) if m.any() else 0.0

results.name: single_example_multiple_yes
results.description: For single-example sets, yes rate for non-example targets that are multiples of the example's smallest factor >1 minus yes rate for non-multiples; observed above null means one example triggers rule generalisation more than the model predicts.
results.code:
# name: single_example_multiple_yes
# description: For single-example sets, yes rate for non-example targets that are multiples of the example's smallest factor >1 minus yes rate for non-multiples; observed above null means one example triggers rule generalisation more than the model predicts.
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    one = ~s.str.contains(",").values
    x = pd.to_numeric(s.where(one, "0")).astype(int).values
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    f = np.zeros_like(x)
    for k in range(9, 1, -1):
        f = np.where((x > 1) & (x % k == 0), k, f)
    ok = one & (f > 1) & (t != x)
    mul = ok & (t % np.maximum(f, 1) == 0)
    r = df["rating"].values
    return float(r[mul].mean() - r[ok & ~mul].mean())

results.name: prime_set_two_target
results.description: Yes rate for target 2 minus yes rate for other prime targets, among sets whose examples (>=2) are all odd primes; observed below null means people reject the even prime 2 more than the prime-rule learner predicts.

results.name: late_session_yes_drop
results.description: Per-participant yes-rate change from the first to the second half of the session (trial_index >=225 minus <225), averaged; observed below null means people grow more conservative over the session than stimulus differences predict.
results.code:
# name: late_session_yes_drop
# description: Per-participant yes-rate change from the first to the second half of the session (trial_index >=225 minus <225), averaged; observed below null means people grow more conservative over the session than stimulus differences predict.
def test_statistic(df):
    pid = (df["trial_index"].values == 0).cumsum()
    late = df["trial_index"].values >= 225
    g = pd.DataFrame({"p": pid, "l": late, "r": df["rating"].values}).groupby(["p", "l"])["r"].mean().unstack()
    return float((g[True] - g[False]).mean())

results.name: odd_set_even_target_yes
results.description: Yes rate for even targets inside the example span for all-odd sets of >=3 examples; observed above null means the model rejects parity-violating in-range targets more than people do.
results.code:
# name: odd_set_even_target_yes
# description: Yes rate for even targets inside the example span for all-odd sets of >=3 examples; observed above null means the model rejects parity-violating in-range targets more than people do.
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",")
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    mat = np.full((len(df), 4), -1)
    for j in range(4):
        mat[:, j] = pd.to_numeric(s.str[j], errors="coerce").fillna(-1).astype(int).values
    valid = mat > 0
    n = valid.sum(1)
    allodd = np.all(~valid | (mat % 2 == 1), 1)
    mn = np.where(valid, mat, 1000).min(1); mx = np.where(valid, mat, -1).max(1)
    m = allodd & (n >= 3) & (t % 2 == 0) & (t > mn) & (t < mx)
    return float(df["rating"].values[m].mean()) if m.any() else 0.0
